question: Identify the Sultan of Delhi who brought Bengal under the control of Delhi Sultanate and appointed his son Bughra Khan as the Governor of Bengal?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Balban**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tughril Khan**, the Bengali governor, rose up in **rebellion** against** Balban** in or around **1279 CE**. Tughril Khan was executed after **Balban** dispatched his troops to** Bengal**.
 
• **Bughra Khan**, the son of Balban, was named **governor of Bengal**.
 
• Balban increased the **monarchy's** authority. He established **strict** court rules and new traditions.
 
• He asserted himself as the **defender** of **Turkish nobility**. He denied non-Turks administrative roles and denied significant government positions to **Muslims** from India.
 
• He hired **spies** and created a successful spy network to keep tabs on the activities of the aristocrats.
 
• He reorganized the army and created a distinct** military department** called **Diwan-e-arz**. To put down the rebellious forces, he dispersed the troops around his nation.
 
• *Therefore, Balban is the Sultan of Delhi who brought Bengal under the control of the Delhi Sultanate and appointed his son Bughra Khan as the Governor of Bengal.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
 

 __**Ruler**__
 __**Description**__
 
 

 **Alauddin Khalji**
 Alauddin Khalji, who later held the title of **Sultan of Delhi**, was one of the Khalji dynasty's most **formidable** kings. He **killed** his **father-in-law** to increase his influence in Delhi.
 
 

 **Muhammad Tughluq**
 He's also renowned for making** radical policy** changes. After his father passed away in 1325, Muhammad took the throne of Delhi. He spoke **multiple languages** and had a keen interest in **medicine.**
 
 

 **Bahlul Lodi**
 The **Lodi Dynasty** was started by Bahlol Lodi. Bahl was a tenacious leader who used his **charismatic** presence to keep a loose alliance of **Turkish and Afghan** rulers together.
